idea:
GitHub issue #45 on mtgibbs/pi-cluster-mcp: Pi-hole stats are primary-only — the secondary is never polled (HA DNS observability gap).

Pi-hole stats are collected from the primary only. PIHOLE_URL is unset, so it defaults to pihole-web, whose Service selector is app: pihole. The secondary runs as app: pihole-secondary and the client has no secondary support, so it is never polled. On our HA DNS (two Pi-hole instances), stats only reflect one of the two resolvers; queries served by the secondary are invisible, and a secondary-only auth/health problem would not show up in get_dns_status. The brainrot CronJob iterates both hosts explicitly (HOSTS="192.168.1.55 192.168.1.56").

Suggested fix: support a list of Pi-hole hosts (env or config), not a single PIHOLE_URL. Authenticate and fetch stats per instance; aggregate totals and/or surface per-instance health so a single-node failure is visible.

===== specs/pihole-secondary-stats/spec.md =====
# Spec: Pi-hole multi-instance stats (primary + secondary)

## 1. Why · [R]

`get_dns_status` reports one of our two HA resolvers. `src/clients/pihole.ts` reads a single
`PIHOLE_URL` that defaults to `http://pihole-web.pihole.svc.cluster.local`, whose Service selects
`app: pihole`; the secondary runs as `app: pihole-secondary` and nothing in the client can reach it.
So queries served by the secondary are invisible in the stats, and a secondary-only auth or health
problem never shows up in `get_dns_status` (the pod list comes from the `pihole` namespace, but the
stats block is primary-only).

## 2. Outcomes · [R]

1. The client polls **every** configured Pi-hole instance, not one. Setting `PIHOLE_URLS` (or
   leaving the default) yields a list of base URLs; each is fetched independently.
2. `getFullStats()` returns a `servers` array with one entry per instance: `url`, `ok`, and either
   the per-instance stats (`summary`, `topQueries`, `topBlocked`, `queryTypes`) or an `error`
   string. Per-instance errors are reported, never thrown into place of the other instances.
3. `getFullStats()` still returns top-level `summary` / `topQueries` / `topBlocked` / `queryTypes`,
   so today's callers keep working. That top-level block is the healthy primary
   (`servers[0]`) when the primary is healthy; when the primary is down it is the first healthy
   secondary plus a top-level `degraded` reason naming the failed instance, so a primary-only
   reader is not silently shown a healthy picture.
4. Aggregates over all healthy instances are exposed as `totals`: `totalQueries`, `blockedQueries`,
   `percentBlocked` (recomputed as `blocked / total * 100`, `0` when `total` is 0),
   `uniqueDomains`, `queriesForwarded`, `queriesCached`, `uniqueClients`, `domainsBeingBlocked`
   (max, not sum — gravity is replicated, so summing would double-count), and
   `healthyServers` / `totalServers`.
5. `get_dns_status` surfaces this: `stats` gains `servers` (per-instance `url`, `ok`, `error`),
   `stats.totals` (the aggregate block), and a top-level `statsDegraded` flag whenever any
   configured instance failed.
6. Auth stays per instance: one session cache and one login single-flight per base URL, so a burst
   of parallel calls performs at most one `POST /api/auth` **per** instance. Rate-limit suppression
   (`429` cooldown) is tracked per instance — the secondary being throttled must not suppress
   logins to the primary.

## 3. Entities · [E]

- Env var `PIHOLE_URLS` (new): comma-separated list of Pi-hole base URLs, whitespace-trimmed,
  empty entries dropped. Falls back to `PIHOLE_URL` when unset/empty; falls back to
  `http://pihole-web.pihole.svc.cluster.local` when neither is set. `PIHOLE_URL` keeps working
  unchanged — single-instance deployments need no config change.
- Env vars unchanged: `PIHOLE_API_TOKEN` / `PIHOLE_PASSWORD` (same password for both instances —
  they share the ESO secret; per-instance credentials are out of scope).
- New exports in `src/clients/pihole.ts`:
  - `export interface PiholeServerStats` — `{ url: string; ok: boolean; error?: string;
    summary?: PiholeStats; topQueries?: { domain: string; count: number }[];
    topBlocked?: { domain: string; count: number }[]; queryTypes?: { type: string; percentage: number }[] }`
  - `export interface PiholeTotals` — the aggregate fields named in Outcome 4.
  - `export function getPiholeUrls(): string[]` — resolved instance list (exported so a test can
    assert the parsing/fallback rules deterministically).
- `getFullStats()` return type `PiholeFullStats` gains `servers: PiholeServerStats[]`,
  `totals: PiholeTotals`, `degraded?: string`.
- Single-instance helpers keep their current signature and hit `PIHOLE_URLS[0]` (the primary):
  `getSummary`, `getTopItems`, `getQueryTypes`, `getStatus`, `getMessages`, `getWhitelist`,
  `getRecentQueries`, `updateGravity`.

## 4. Approach · [A]

Turn the module-level singletons into per-URL state: a `Map<url, { sessionId, expiry }>` plus a
`Map<url, inFlightLogin>` and a `Map<url, rateLimitedUntil>`, keyed by base URL, created lazily
inside `authenticate(url)`. `piholeFetch(endpoint, url, requiresAuth)` takes the target URL.
`getFullStats()` fans out with `Promise.allSettled` over `getPiholeUrls()`, and each per-instance
promise runs `getSummary` / `getTopItems` / `getQueryTypes` for that URL — so one dead instance
costs one failed entry, not the whole tool. `totals` is computed by summing the healthy instances
(recomputing `percentBlocked` from summed numerator/denominator rather than averaging percentages),
and the top-level `summary` block is `servers[0]` when healthy, else the first healthy server with
`degraded` set. Rejected alternatives: (a) a second `PIHOLE_SECONDARY_URL` constant — hardcodes a
topology of exactly two and doubles every future edit; (b) a `PiholeClient` class with constructor
injection — a needless rewrite of every call site and test for what is currently module state;
(c) an always-on background poller that caches stats — new lifecycle/timer surface, and the tools
are on-demand; (d) load-balancing reads across instances behind one URL — hides which instance is
broken, which is the actual complaint.

## 5. Scope · [S]

In scope:
- `src/clients/pihole.ts` — per-URL auth/fetch, `PIHOLE_URLS`, multi-instance `getFullStats`,
  `getPiholeUrls`, `PiholeServerStats`, `PiholeTotals`.
- `src/tools/dns.ts` — `get_dns_status` only: add `stats.servers`, `stats.totals`, `statsDegraded`.
- `src/__tests__/pihole-multi-instance.test.ts` (new).

Out of scope: `k8s/` manifests, `package.json`, CI, auth scopes, tool registration/count,
`update_pihole_gravity` (primary-only write stays primary-only), `get_pihole_whitelist` /
`get_pihole_queries` / `get_dns_messages`-style single-instance readers, `diagnose_dns` and
`test_dns_query` (exec-based, not HTTP), per-instance credentials, any new dependency.

## 6. Prior facts · [S]

- `src/clients/pihole.ts:4-5` reads `PIHOLE_URL` / `PIHOLE_API_TOKEN||PIHOLE_PASSWORD` into
  module consts at import time; tests therefore re-import the module (`vi.resetModules()` +
  dynamic `import('../clients/pihole.js')`) and `vi.stubEnv` before — see
  `src/__tests__/pihole-auth.test.ts:42-46`.
- `src/clients/pihole.ts:124-163` — `authenticate()` single-flights login via `authInFlight` and
  honours a `rateLimitedUntil` cooldown; `login()` (174-229) throws on 401/invalid session and on
  429, distinguishing throttling from a bad credential. Those messages and that distinction are
  load-bearing (`#44`, `#48`) and must survive unchanged, including the `sid` header on
  `stats/summary`.
- `getFullStats()` (470-492) is the only multi-endpoint caller: `getSummary` + `getTopItems` (2
  `stats/top_domains` calls) + `getQueryTypes` (another `stats/summary`). `get_dns_status`
  (`src/tools/dns.ts:68-101`) calls `getFullStats(5)` and `getMessages()` in parallel inside a
  `try`, storing any throw as `result.statsError`, and flattens `stats.summary.*` into
  `queriesToday` / `blockedToday` / `blockedPercentage` / `domainsBlocked` / `uniqueDomains` /
  `queriesForwarded` / `queriesCached` / `uniqueClients` / `gravityUpdated` plus `topQueries` /
  `topBlocked`. Those keys must keep their meaning, and `result.stats` has no `servers` or `totals`
  key today.
- `src/tools/dns.ts:34-41` already lists every pod in the `pihole` namespace whose name contains
  `pihole` and not `unbound`, so the secondary pod is already in `result.pihole` — which is exactly
  why the stats gap reads as a contradiction: healthy pods, single-node numbers.
- `updateGravity()` (440-461) posts `/api/action/gravity`; the whitelist is `pihole/pihole`
  (CLAUDE.md), so gravity stays primary-only.
- CLAUDE.md norms that apply: read-only tools stay read-only; no secrets in output; `describe_*`
  style redaction exists because responses are shown to a model; summary-first output is the
  house style (`src/utils/summary.ts`) — tools pre-compute verdicts rather than dumping raw data.

## 7. Norms · [N]

- Errors are strings in tool results (`{ error, code, message }`); clients throw `Error` with a
  message that names the cause and the fix. Per-instance failures become `error` fields on that
  instance's entry, not thrown exceptions.
- Keep the 429-vs-bad-credential wording: a throttled instance must say "rate-limiting"/"suppressed"
  and must NOT say "must equal the Pi-hole web password".
- Every per-instance error message includes the base URL, so a reader knows which resolver is sick.
- Tests: vitest, `vi.stubGlobal('fetch', …)` returning real `Response` objects, fresh module import
  per test, no network, no timers. Follow `src/__tests__/pihole-auth.test.ts` style: a comment
  block explaining the live failure the test guards.
- No new dependencies; TypeScript strict; `npm run lint` and `npm run typecheck` must stay clean.

## 8. Safeguards · [S]

- No credentials in any log or response: error strings may contain the base URL and Pi-hole's error
  key/message, never `PIHOLE_PASSWORD` / `PIHOLE_API_TOKEN` or the request body.
- No new write path: only `GET`s fan out per instance. `updateGravity` must not start POSTing to
  every instance.
- No fail-open: a failing instance must appear as `ok: false` with an `error` and must lower
  `totals.healthyServers` below `totals.totalServers` (and set `statsDegraded`). Silently skipping
  an unreachable instance is the exact bug being fixed.
- No fail-closed either: one unreachable instance must not make `get_dns_status` return
  `statsError` with no numbers — the healthy instance's data still has to be reported.
- Single-instance deployments (only `PIHOLE_URL` set, or nothing set) must behave exactly as today:
  same URL fetched, one login, same `stats.*` keys.
- Do not regress the `#44` / `#48` guarantees: `sid` header on `stats/summary`, loud auth failure,
  one shared login per burst — now scoped per instance.

## 9. Tasks · [O]

```
T1: In src/clients/pihole.ts, resolve the instance list from PIHOLE_URLS (comma-separated, trimmed,
    empty dropped) falling back to PIHOLE_URL then the pihole-web default, export getPiholeUrls(),
    and move the session cache, login single-flight and 429 cooldown into per-base-URL state.
T2: In src/clients/pihole.ts, make piholeFetch/updateGravity take a target URL and rewrite
    getFullStats() to fan out per instance with Promise.allSettled, returning servers, totals and
    a degraded reason while keeping the existing top-level summary/topQueries/topBlocked/queryTypes
    keys, and exporting PiholeServerStats and PiholeTotals.
T3: In src/tools/dns.ts, add stats.servers, stats.totals and a top-level statsDegraded flag to
    get_dns_status without changing the existing stats.* keys.
T4: Add src/__tests__/pihole-multi-instance.test.ts with the four tests named in §11.
```

## 10. Acceptance criteria (EARS) · [O]

- AC1. When `PIHOLE_URLS` is set to two URLs, the system shall request `/api/auth` and
  `stats/summary` once per URL for a `getFullStats()` call. → `polls every configured Pi-hole and
  reports per-instance stats`
- AC2. If one instance returns 500 (or its login fails), then the system shall still return the
  other instance's stats at top level, mark the failing entry `ok: false` with an error naming its
  URL, and set `totals.healthyServers` to 1 of 2. → `marks an unreachable secondary as failed …`
- AC3. When more than one instance is healthy, the system shall set `totals.totalQueries` to the
  sum of their `dns_queries_today`, `totals.blockedQueries` to the sum of `ads_blocked_today`, and
  `totals.percentBlocked` to `blocked / total * 100` (not an average of the per-instance
  percentages). → `aggregates query totals across both instances …`
- AC4. When a burst of concurrent `getFullStats()` calls runs against two instances, the system
  shall perform exactly one `POST /api/auth` per instance. → `performs one login per instance for a
  burst of concurrent calls`
- AC5. If `PIHOLE_URLS` is unset, then the system shall behave as today: one instance, the
  `PIHOLE_URL` (or pihole-web) base URL, and the existing top-level stats keys. → covered by AC1's
  sibling default-path assertion inside `polls every configured Pi-hole…` and by the untouched
  `src/__tests__/pihole-auth.test.ts` suite.

## 11. Verification

`verify.sh` runs five checks (the last one is reported twice in the gate output because the
client/tool identifier checks are grouped per file), all of which fail on today's tree:

1. **New test file exists** — `src/__tests__/pihole-multi-instance.test.ts` is present. Fails today:
   the file does not exist. Proves the tests were written rather than the code quietly changed.
2. **Test titles present** — greps the file for the exact titles `polls every configured Pi-hole
   and reports per-instance stats`, `marks an unreachable secondary as failed without hiding the
   primary`, `aggregates query totals across both instances and recomputes percent blocked`,
   `performs one login per instance for a burst of concurrent calls`. Fails today (no file);
   catches an implementation that skips the aggregation or per-instance-login cases.
3. **New names exported/used** — greps `src/clients/pihole.ts` for `PIHOLE_URLS`, `getPiholeUrls`,
   `PiholeServerStats`, `PiholeTotals` and `src/tools/dns.ts` for `statsDegraded` / `totals`.
   Fails today: none of those identifiers exist.
4. **Targeted test run** — `npx vitest run src/__tests__/pihole-multi-instance.test.ts` must exit 0.
   Fails today: vitest errors on the missing file; later it fails if the fan-out, allSettled error
   isolation, aggregate math, or per-instance single-flight login is wrong.
5. **Regression guard** — `npx vitest run src/__tests__/pihole-auth.test.ts` must still exit 0: the
   per-instance refactor must not break the `#44` (sid header, loud auth failure) or `#48`
   (single-flight login, 429 cooldown) guarantees. It reports FAIL until check 1's test file
   exists, so it can never be the lone thing holding up the gate on an unimplemented tree.

`verify.sh` was run against the pre-change tree: all 6 checks FAIL (no test file, no titles, no
`PIHOLE_URLS`/`getPiholeUrls`/`PiholeServerStats`/`PiholeTotals`, no `servers`/`totals`/
`statsDegraded` in `src/tools/dns.ts`, vitest finds no test file, regression guard gated). Every
check is tied to an identifier or test this change introduces, so none can pass by accident.

## 12. Open questions

- Do both instances share the same web password today (single `pihole-password` secret key in
  `k8s/deployment.yaml`)? The spec assumes yes and keeps one credential; if they diverge, a
  `PIHOLE_PASSWORDS` list is the follow-up (deliberately out of scope here).
- Whether `get_pihole_queries` / `get_pihole_whitelist` should merge across instances: left for a
  later spec to keep this one small.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Gate for spec: pihole-secondary-stats (issue #45)
# Run from the repo root as: STRICT=1 bash specs/pihole-secondary-stats/verify.sh
# Offline and deterministic: no network, no cluster, no secrets.

set -uo pipefail
cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"

CLIENT=src/clients/pihole.ts
TOOL=src/tools/dns.ts
TEST=src/__tests__/pihole-multi-instance.test.ts
REGRESSION=src/__tests__/pihole-auth.test.ts

FAILURES=0

report() {
  # report <label> <ok(0|1)> <detail>
  local label="$1" ok="$2" detail="$3"
  if [ "$ok" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "PASS: $label"
  else
    echo "FAIL: $label — $detail"
    FAILURES=$((FAILURES + 1))
  fi
}

# --- Check 1: the new test file exists -------------------------------------
if [ -f "$TEST" ]; then
  report "$TEST exists" 0 ''
else
  report "$TEST exists" 1 "no multi-instance test file was added"
fi

# --- Check 2: the named test titles exist ----------------------------------
missing_titles=""
for title in \
  "polls every configured Pi-hole and reports per-instance stats" \
  "marks an unreachable secondary as failed without hiding the primary" \
  "aggregates query totals across both instances and recomputes percent blocked" \
  "performs one login per instance for a burst of concurrent calls"; do
  if [ -f "$TEST" ] && ! grep -qF "it('$title'" "$TEST"; then
    missing_titles="$missing_titles '$title'"
  fi
done
if [ ! -f "$TEST" ]; then
  report "required it() titles present in $TEST" 1 "test file missing, so no titles to check"
elif [ -z "$missing_titles" ]; then
  report "required it() titles present in $TEST" 0 ''
else
  report "required it() titles present in $TEST" 1 "missing:$missing_titles"
fi

# --- Check 3: new config/export names in the client ------------------------
missing_names=""
for name in PIHOLE_URLS getPiholeUrls PiholeServerStats PiholeTotals; do
  if [ -f "$CLIENT" ] && ! grep -q "$name" "$CLIENT"; then
    missing_names="$missing_names $name"
  fi
done
if [ ! -f "$CLIENT" ]; then
  report "$CLIENT declares PIHOLE_URLS/getPiholeUrls/PiholeServerStats/PiholeTotals" 1 "client file missing"
elif [ -z "$missing_names" ]; then
  report "$CLIENT declares PIHOLE_URLS/getPiholeUrls/PiholeServerStats/PiholeTotals" 0 ''
else
  report "$CLIENT declares PIHOLE_URLS/getPiholeUrls/PiholeServerStats/PiholeTotals" 1 "missing:$missing_names"
fi

# --- Check 4: get_dns_status surfaces per-instance health + totals ---------
missing_dns=""
for name in servers totals statsDegraded; do
  if [ -f "$TOOL" ] && ! grep -q "$name" "$TOOL"; then
    missing_dns="$missing_dns $name"
  fi
done
if [ ! -f "$TOOL" ]; then
  report "$TOOL surfaces stats.servers/stats.totals/statsDegraded" 1 "dns tool file missing"
elif [ -z "$missing_dns" ]; then
  report "$TOOL surfaces stats.servers/stats.totals/statsDegraded" 0 ''
else
  report "$TOOL surfaces stats.servers/stats.totals/statsDegraded" 1 "missing:$missing_dns"
fi

# --- Check 5: the new tests actually pass ---------------------------------
if npx vitest run "$TEST" >/tmp/verify-multi-instance.log 2>&1; then
  report "npx vitest run $TEST" 0 ''
else
  report "npx vitest run $TEST" 1 "see /tmp/verify-multi-instance.log (tail below)"
  tail -n 25 /tmp/verify-multi-instance.log | sed 's/^/    /'
fi

# --- Check 6: auth regressions (#44 sid header, #48 single-flight) still pass.
# Only once the new tests exist: before the change there is no refactor to regress on,
# and this check must not be the only thing standing between a broken implementation
# and a green gate.
if [ ! -f "$TEST" ]; then
  report "npx vitest run $REGRESSION (no auth regression)" 1 "$TEST missing — nothing to regress-check yet"
elif npx vitest run "$REGRESSION" >/tmp/verify-pihole-auth.log 2>&1; then
  report "npx vitest run $REGRESSION (no auth regression)" 0 ''
else
  report "npx vitest run $REGRESSION (no auth regression)" 1 "see /tmp/verify-pihole-auth.log (tail below)"
  tail -n 25 /tmp/verify-pihole-auth.log | sed 's/^/    /'
fi

echo
if [ "$FAILURES" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "verify.sh: all checks passed"
  exit 0
fi
echo "verify.sh: $FAILURES check(s) failed"
exit 1
